newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan premier barred from parliament in nuke row.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan premier barred from parliament in nuke row.

text.p: Opposition deputies on Tuesday blocked Premier Lien Chan's entry to parliament to appeal for restored funding for Taiwan's fourth nuclear power project, a move Lien angrily denounced as anti-democratic.
"This is a dark day for democracy," Lien was quoted by the state-funded Central News Agency as saying after the rebuff.
State television showed an angry Lien giving a "thumbs down" gesture before being whisked away by limousine.
The premier had planned to deliver a report explaining the government's energy policy -- and the island's need for a fourth nuclear station -- as parliament resumed debate on the project.

But dozens of opposition lawmakers, cheered by thousands of anti-nuclear demonstrators, donned green headbands and locked arms to form human walls outside the building's three entrances, preventing Lien and other cabinet officials from entering.
Lien immediately returned to his office.

Parliament on May 24 dealt an embarrassing blow to Taipei's nuclear energy policy, halting the 2,700-megawatt plant's US$4.1 billion budget on the very day of Taiwan Power Co's final tender for the facility's two reactors.
The cabinet formally appealed the cancellation on June 6 but can be thwarted by a two-thirds vote of parliament -- something Lien and other officials are determined to avoid.
Hanging in the balance, among other jobs, is the fate of a US$1.8 billion contract awarded to U.S. giant General Electric to supply the power plant's twin reactors and turbines.
"Construction of the fourth nuclear power plant is a vital national policy," government spokesman Su Chi told state radio.
"The government has a responsibility and obligation to explain the policy," Su said of Lien's planned speech.
The parliament was in a recess but would resume later in the day.
